title: Untangle orchestrator lane separation and KV stabilization
creator: Amina Patel
description: Summary: Reduce tail latency variance and eliminate cross-lane interference by decomposing the orchestrator into explicit lane-separated execution paths and stabilizing the KV cache read path. Background: Over the past year we have accumulated fixes in the orchestrator that multiplex multiple admission patterns and KV cache warmup logic into a single codepath. This led to unpredictable batch composition during bursts, KV hotkey thrash, and complex lock contention in the scheduler. Goals: 1) Separate fast-path latency-sensitive lanes (short-seq low-token requests) from throughput lanes (long-seq, high-token requests). 2) Replace the shared KV priming logic with a lane-aware prefetcher that exposes deterministic TTL semantics and reduces concurrent eviction churn. 3) Simplify scheduler decision points to three well-documented hooks: admit(), prioritize(), and preempt(). 4) Ship without API changes and maintain zero-downtime rollout for hosted and dedicated modes.
acceptance_criteria: Deployed lane-separated orchestrator with runtime flag to opt-in per-tenant
KV prefetcher implements TTL and per-lane reservation and reduces eviction spikes by >= 40% in synthetic hotkey test
P99 request latency reduced by at least 12% on tail-sensitive benchmark (same load profile)
No regressions in functional tests for session affinity, streaming, and function calling (CI green)
Can rollback to existing orchestrator by flipping runtime flag without session loss
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Introduce lane abstraction and API surface (admit/prioritize/preempt) behind feature flag
Phase 2: Implement lane-aware KV prefetcher and TTL contract; add metrics for reservation occupancy and eviction_reason
Phase 3: Migrate one non-critical tenant to throughput lane for 48h soak; collect telemetry and compare to baseline
Phase 4: Iterate on prefetch heuristic (window sizes, lookahead) based on telemetry; run regression perf suite
Phase 5: Promote feature flag to default and deprecate legacy multiplexer after 2 weeks of production telemetry
testing_plan: Unit: cover lane admission code with exhaustive branch tests for edge cases (timeout, cancel, max_tokens)
Integration: end-to-end using local docker runtime with KV snapshotting enabled; verify warmup sequence and eviction patterns
Performance: run canonical tail-sensitivity benchmark (100k requests across mixes) and hotkey churn test used in infra team dashboard
Chaos: simulate KV eviction stalls and node preemption using test harness; ensure graceful fallback to conservative lane
Canary: rollout to 5% hosted capacity, compare error budget burn and latency curves over 72h
rollback_plan: Feature flag toggles to previous orchestrator within control plane. If canary shows >20% latency regression or any functional failure, flip flag and run automated session drain script. Escalate to oncall and pause all Dedicated rollouts until validation.
metrics: Baseline KV eviction spikes: observed 110 evictions/min during synthetic hotkey run (target <= 65 evictions/min)
Batch fill ratio: target improvement of +8 percentage points on short-seq lane
Error budget burn: maintain <5% increase during 72h canary

notes: Trade-offs: stronger lane isolation increases code complexity but reduces cross-tenant noise. We accept a small increase in scheduler code surface area to get deterministic behavior.
Decision: Keep KV priming TTL configurable per-tenant; default to aggressive warmup for latency-sensitive tenants.
Follow-up: Post-launch item to add adaptive lookahead based on request histograms (future ticket)
Observation: Some legacy tenants rely on the old batch-merge heuristics; plan a compatibility validation phase before full rollout
